chunks: From Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, that he said:

The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم went out to the prayer while al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام had been delayed in speaking, to the point that they feared he would not speak and that there might be muteness in him. So he صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم went out with him, carrying him on his shoulder, and the people formed rows behind him. He placed him on his right side. Then the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم began the prayer, and al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام said the takbīr. When the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم heard his takbīr, he repeated it and al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام said the takbīr, until the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said seven takbīrs and al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام said the takbīr. Thus the sunnah proceeded according to that.

key_terms.السُّنَّةُ: the established prophetic practice derived from this event
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: the ritual prayer being performed in congregation
key_terms.الْحُسَيْنُ: Imam al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام, present with the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم in this report
key_terms.الْكَلَامِ: speech, whose delay in appearing caused concern
key_terms.تَكْبِيرَهُ: his utterance of the takbīr in the prayer
key_terms.خَرَسٌ: muteness or speech impediment that people feared might affect him
key_terms.سَبْعَ تَكْبِيرَاتٍ: seven takbīrs at the opening of the prayer
key_terms.عَاتِقِهِ: his shoulder, on which the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم carried al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام

ai.seo_question: What is the origin of saying seven takbīrs at the beginning of the prayer in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم brought al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام to the prayer and repeated the opening takbīr with him until they reached seven takbīrs. The report presents the origin of the practice of seven opening takbīrs in prayer and also reflects the special care shown to al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام.
